about_p1: I'm Gonzalo — Nyasper on GitHub. I'm a self-taught web developer with four years of self-study. I haven't worked professionally in the industry yet, but I've spent years building projects, learning continuously, and refining my skills. No CS degree, no bootcamp — just curiosity and more broken projects than I'd like to admit. That journey is what brought me here.
about_p2: Most of my experience is within the JavaScript ecosystem, although I enjoy exploring new technologies and tools whenever I can.
about_p3_before: If you made it this far — thanks. Seriously. I hope something here caught your attention.
faq_q1_question: What keeps me hooked on coding?
faq_q1_answer: Programming feels like a game where every bug is a boss fight and every project unlocks a new skill tree. I started because I was curious, but I stayed because I enjoy the process of building things and figuring out how they work.
faq_q2_question: What do I enjoy most about programming?
faq_q2_answer: That moment when something finally clicks after hours of being completely lost. Your brain was working the whole time without telling you — and then, out of nowhere, it just hands you the answer. Also the fact that the ceiling doesn't exist. There's always a deeper layer, a better pattern, something you hadn't considered, no matter how much you learn, there's always another level waiting.
faq_q3_answer: "Nyasper" is the Japanese name of Espurr — a Pokémon. That psychic cat with an existential stare on my GitHub profile picture. Somehow the name just stuck with me.
faq_q4_question: Why so many frameworks? Are you an expert in all of them?
faq_q4_answer: Definitely not an expert in all of them — and that's kind of the point. I believe knowing a tool exists is half the battle. You don't need to master everything, but you need to know when to reach for it. A carpenter doesn't use the same tool for every job.
faq_q5_answer: Not because it's trendy. I use it because it gets out of my way. Less boilerplate, cleaner code, and it makes building feel closer to thinking. Once you write a component in Svelte, going back feels like typing with oven mitts.
faq_q6_question: What about .NET? Didn't you specialize in the JS ecosystem?
faq_q6_answer: JavaScript was my entry point, but C# and .NET is where I actually learned to think like a developer. OOP, design patterns, dependency injection — concepts that changed how I approach every problem, regardless of the language. It doesn't get the spotlight on this portfolio, but it has a permanent place in how I think.
faq_q7_answer: I think it's the most interesting and uncomfortable shift the industry has seen in a while. AI isn't replacing developers — it's redefining what one developer can do alone. I'd rather be someone who adapts than someone who complains, and honestly, I'm curious where this goes.
faq_q8_question: What's something programming taught me outside of coding?
faq_q8_answer: Probably patience. Debugging teaches you very quickly that being frustrated doesn't solve problems — understanding them does.
